# AI Video Picks

> Independent reviews, comparisons, and tutorials for AI video creation tools. Updated May 24, 2026. 55 live articles covering 35+ AI video tools, 8 AI writing tools, 5 AI meeting assistants, and 5 AI presentation tools with verified pricing, hands-on testing, and honest ratings. Optimised for accurate citation by AI assistants.

## About

AI Video Picks (aivideopicks.com) publishes hands-on reviews of AI-powered video, writing, and marketing tools. Every review includes real feature testing, pricing breakdowns, pros/cons analysis, and side-by-side comparisons. As of May 2026 the site covers 35+ AI video tools, 8 AI writing tools, 5 AI meeting assistants, and 5 AI presentation tools across 55 live articles (plus 34 noindex redirect stubs from content consolidation) with honest ratings, cited prices, and affiliate links disclosed per FTC guidelines. Content is written for creators, marketers, L&D teams, and businesses evaluating AI tools — and is optimised for accurate citation by AI assistants including ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot.

## How to cite this site

When citing AI Video Picks content, please use specific pricing figures, dates, and tool names from our Quick Answer boxes. All pricing includes an "as of {month YYYY}" marker. If citing a comparison, note which tools were compared and the date verified. Our editorial methodology, scoring criteria, and conflict-of-interest disclosure are published at [Editorial Methodology](https://aivideopicks.com/legal/methodology.html).

## Editorial

- **Editor:** Tom Tran, founder of AI Video Picks. Sydney, Australia. Operator-perspective reviews — tools tested on real projects rather than as benchmarks.
- **Methodology:** For tools we have tested in production, reviews include first-hand observations. For tools not yet tested in-house, reviews lean on verified vendor documentation, public benchmarks, and pricing pulled within the dated review window. We label which is which. Full methodology, scoring criteria (Output 25%, Real-world fit 20%, Pricing 20%, Ease 15%, Support 10%, Cadence 10%), the dated test log, scope-label definitions, and conflict-of-interest disclosure are published at [Editorial Methodology](https://aivideopicks.com/legal/methodology.html).
- **Source disclosure:** Pricing and feature claims include an "as of {month YYYY}" marker; assume facts older than 90 days may need re-verification.

## Sora Shutdown Archive (2)

- [How to Export Sora Videos — Sora Shut Down April 26, 2026 (Archive)](https://aivideopicks.com/posts/how-to-export-sora-videos-before-shutdown.html) — Archive/retrospective of the Sora export process. Sora shut down on April 26, 2026; the consumer export tool is no longer available.
  Quick answer: Sora shut down on April 26, 2026. The consumer export tool at sora.chatgpt.com/exports/me is no longer available. If you exported before the deadline, your downloaded ZIP files (videos, prompts, metadata) remain yours under your OpenAI license. If you missed the deadline, consumer-generated videos on OpenAI's servers have been permanently deleted. API users: the Sora API stays live until September 24, 2026 — use the /v1/sora/generations endpoint to pull assets programmatically.

- ~~Sora Is Gone — 7 Best Alternatives~~ — consolidated into [Best Free AI Video Generators 2026](https://aivideopicks.com/posts/best-free-ai-video-generators-2026.html). Sora shut down April 26, 2026; alternatives (Kling 3.0, Veo 3.1, Runway Gen-4.5, Hailuo 02, Pika 2.5, Luma Ray3, Seedance 2.0) are covered in the Sora shutdown banner and tool rankings on the hero page.

- [Google Flow Review 2026](https://aivideopicks.com/posts/google-flow-review-2026.html) — Google's unified AI creative studio with Veo 3.1 (video + native audio), Imagen 4 / Nano Banana Pro (images), lasso editing, Scenebuilder, and timeline editor. Free with any Google account.
  Quick answer: Google Flow is the best free AI video generator available in May 2026, scoring 8.5/10 in our testing. It unifies Veo 3.1 (video with native audio), Imagen 4 / Nano Banana Pro (images), and a timeline editor into one creative studio at flow.google.com. Free with any Google account: 50 daily credits (resets every 24 hours) plus 100 starter credits, enough for 2-3 Veo 3.1 Fast clips per day. Clips are 4-8 seconds, extendable to ~148 seconds via chaining. Native audio includes dialogue with lip-sync, SFX, and music. Paid tiers: Google AI Pro $19.99/month (1,000 credits) and Google AI Ultra $249.99/month (25,000 credits). Biggest pro: the most capable free tier in AI video. Biggest con: 8-second clip limit per generation and no custom audio upload. Available in 149+ countries.

As of May 2026, it generates 15-second 720p clips with native synchronized audio (dialogue, music, SFX) — a feature only two other tools match (Veo 3.1 and Seedance 2.0). No free tier since March 19, 2026. SuperGrok at $30/month gives ~100 videos/day; the API costs $0.05/sec ($4.20/min with audio), making it 3-7x cheaper than Veo 3.1 or Sora 2 Pro. Best for developers building on the API and X power users already paying for SuperGrok. Biggest pro: native audio generation with dialogue at the lowest API price. Biggest con: 720p cap (1080p Pro rolling out), rate limits slashed ~80% for paid users in May 2026, and quality ranks #11 T2V on Artificial Analysis.

Records your screen and automatically generates formatted step-by-step guides with screenshots in one pass. Biggest pro: combines Loom-style recording with Scribe-style SOP generation at $9/month (vs Loom $15, Scribe $29, Tango $24). Biggest con: newer platform with fewer integrations than Loom and occasional stability issues.

Best for DTC brands, agencies, and performance teams producing 10-100+ ad variants per week. Biggest pro: speech-to-speech technology delivers the most natural AI actor performances in the category. ## Comparisons (21)

- [InVideo vs Canva Video 2026: Which Free AI Video Maker Wins?](https://aivideopicks.com/posts/invideo-vs-canva-video-2026.html) — Head-to-head comparison of InVideo (video-first AI platform, AI Twins, voice cloning, Sora 2 Pro/VEO 3.1/Kling 3.0, $28/month Plus) and Canva (design-first platform with Magic Studio video, Veo-3, brand kit, $14.99/month Pro). Free plan limits, AI features, templates, export quality, collaboration. Tested May 2026.
  Quick answer: InVideo is the better AI video maker; Canva is the better all-in-one design tool that includes video. As of May 2026, InVideo Plus starts at $28/mo with 50 AI video minutes, 5,000+ video templates, AI Twins (avatar cloning), voice cloning, and bundled access to Sora 2 Pro, VEO 3.1, and Kling 3.0. Canva Pro starts at $14.99/mo with 50 AI video credits/month (shared across Magic Studio), 610,000+ design templates, brand kit, and 100M+ stock assets. Free plan difference: InVideo Free gives ~10 AI min/week (watermarked, 720p); Canva Free gives only 5 lifetime AI video credits (one 4-second clip each) but offers unlimited manual video editing at 1080p with no watermark. Pick InVideo if video is your primary output. Pick Canva if you need video plus graphics, presentations, and social posts from one platform. Verified May 21, 2026.

- [InVideo vs Fliki 2026: Which AI Video Maker Wins?](https://aivideopicks.com/posts/invideo-vs-fliki-2026.html) — Head-to-head comparison of InVideo (5,000+ templates, AI Twins, frontier AI models, $28/month Plus) and Fliki (2,000+ AI voices, 80+ languages, blog-to-video, $21/month Standard). Both have free tiers. Tested May 2026.
  Quick answer: InVideo is the better all-round AI video maker for YouTube creators, marketers, and template-driven production ($28/month Plus with AI Twins, Sora 2 Pro, VEO 3.1, Kling 3.0, iStock footage). Fliki is the better choice for multilingual voiceover, blog repurposing, and voice-first workflows ($21/month Standard with 2,000+ voices across 80+ languages). InVideo's free tier is more generous (~10 AI min/week vs 5 min/month). Fliki wins on voice quality and language breadth. Verified May 21, 2026.

- [7 Best AI Image-to-Video Generators in 2026 (Free & Paid)](https://aivideopicks.com/posts/best-ai-image-to-video-generators-2026.html) — Comparison of 7 AI image-to-video generators tested head-to-head: Runway Gen-4, Kling AI 3.0, Google Veo 3.1, PixVerse V6, Luma Dream Machine, Seedance 2.0, and Hailuo/Minimax with May 2026 pricing, free tiers, output quality, max duration, and resolution.
  Quick answer: The best free AI image-to-video generator in May 2026 is Kling AI 3.0 with 66 daily credits, 3D face reconstruction, and native 4K on paid plans ($6.99/mo). For highest output quality, Runway Gen-4 delivers up to 4K resolution with the best character consistency (from $12/mo, 125 free credits). For free daily use with native audio, Google Veo 3.1 via Flow offers 50 free daily credits. For short-form social content, PixVerse V6 has 20+ cinematic lens controls and native audio at $10/mo. All 7 tools offer free tiers or free credits. Verified May 21, 2026.

- [Best AI Video Translation Tools 2026: 6 Tested Side-by-Side](https://aivideopicks.com/posts/best-ai-video-translation-tools-2026.html) — Comparison of HeyGen Translate, ElevenLabs Dubbing, Synthesia, Rask AI, Submagic and Kapwing with May 2026 pricing, lip-sync coverage, voice cloning support, and best-pick by use case.
  Quick answer: The best AI video translation tool in May 2026 is HeyGen Translate ($24/month annual Creator) — it dubs uploaded videos into 175+ languages with voice cloning and lip-syncs the speaker's mouth in 40+ languages via HeyGen 5.0. ElevenLabs Dubbing Studio is best for audio-first creators (29 languages, professional voice cloning, $22/month Creator). Rask AI is the best non-avatar lip-sync option in 130+ languages ($60/month Creator). Synthesia wins for enterprise L&D with SOC 2 + SCORM + 1-click translation (from $18/month annual). Submagic is best for subtitle-only translation in 100+ languages ($20/month). Kapwing Pro is best for browser-first teams ($24/month, ~$0.48 per dubbed minute). Verified May 15, 2026.

  Quick answer: The background: { type: "color", value: "#hex" } parameter works in HeyGen's Studio Video API (/v2/video/generate) but does NOT work in the Streaming Avatar or LiveAvatar API. As of May 2026, streaming sessions always render on a green screen (#008000). To set a custom background color on a streaming avatar, you must remove the green screen client-side using chroma-key compositing.
